data.title: The Foundation
data.content:
Dungeon Theory began as a community built around a simple idea: every run has something to teach.

A small group of Albion Online adventurers gathered in Discord, united by the belief that dungeon mastery comes not from raw power, but from understanding. They shared guides, dissected mechanics, and welcomed questions that others might dismiss.

What started as a handful of players grew into a place where veterans taught newcomers, where failed runs became data, and where the phrase "learn together, grow together" wasn't just a motto—it was the method.

data.title: The Guild Is Born
data.content:
Dungeon Theory evolved beyond a community and established itself as a guild.

The Sworn Order formed—adventurers who didn't just study the theory but lived it. They committed to consistent play, dedicated parties, and long-term progression together. The guild wasn't a separate entity from the community; it was the community taking the next step.

Guild-exclusive activities began: coordinated progression weeks, theory-crafting sessions, and a shared identity. To be Theorybound became a distinction earned through dedication.

data.title: The First Hundred
data.summary: The community reaches its first major milestone.
data.content:
Dungeon Theory reached 100 members.

The milestone marked more than a number. It showed that the idea of learning, improving, and playing together had found a community willing to grow with it. Guides were written. Parties formed daily. The archive of knowledge expanded.

Each new member brought a question, a perspective, or a willingness to teach. The hundred weren't just names on a roster—they were the foundation of what would become the Theorybound.

data.title: The Archive Opens
data.summary: Dungeon Theory establishes its presence beyond Discord.
data.content:
The Dungeon Theory website launches, creating a permanent home for the community's accumulated knowledge.

No longer confined to chat history and pinned messages, the guides, strategies, and stories found a structured archive. The Chronicles page you're reading now became the official historical record.

This wasn't just a website launch. It was a statement: Dungeon Theory is here to stay. The journey has a past worth preserving and a future worth building.
